An industry where one firm can supply the whole market at lower average cost than several firms, e.g. water pipes or a power grid.

front: Effect of one firm on price, quality, choice and profit
back: Higher price, possibly lower quality, less choice, abnormal profit in the long run.
Economies of scale, research funded by profits, no duplication of infrastructure, stability.
Higher prices, restricted output, less choice, little incentive to be efficient, exploitation of consumers.

front: Why is monopoly a market failure?
back: It restricts supply and raises price, so too few resources are used to make the product.

front: Can a monopoly set both price and quantity?
back: No. It sets one; demand then decides the other. A higher price means lower sales.
Competition policy, price and quality regulation, public ownership, removing barriers to entry.
